field.label: WAN Interface
field.help: Select the WAN interface where DPI bypass should be applied.

field.label: Divert Port
field.help: Internal port for ipfw divert socket (default: 989). Change only if conflicting with another service.

field.label: How to find your strategy
field.text:
Run blockcheck2 from the Diagnostics page or via SSH:
cd /usr/local/etc/zapret2 && env IFACE_WAN=your_wan_if /bin/sh blockcheck2.sh

Review the working strategy from the SUMMARY output and add the required profile to the unified Traffic Strategy field below.
HTTP, HTTPS/TLS, TCP and UDP profiles may coexist in the same strategy. Separate independent profiles with --new. Do not replace an existing multi-profile strategy without reviewing how the new profile should be merged.

field.label: Traffic Strategy
field.help:
Native dvtws2 strategy. Independent profiles are separated by --new; the first eligible profile is chosen in engine order. The same HOSTLIST/IPSET target may be used by different profiles.
A single profile may contain multiple ordered --payload and --lua-desync actions. Do not split them with --new unless you intend independent profiles.
--filter-tcp/--filter-udp select profile ports and contribute to IPFW interception coverage; --filter-l7 selects the protocol. Range, payload and Lua actions belong to their profile.
Managed targets: <HOSTLIST:youtube>, <HOSTLIST:user>, <IPSET:telegram>. Do not reference the same resolved list file of the same type twice inside one profile. Native dry-run checks syntax/runtime support; it does not prove DPI bypass.

field.label: Extra Arguments
field.help: Appended after Traffic Strategy in the final dvtws2 command line. Not necessarily global: profile-scoped options can apply to the last profile. Review the combined command before changing this field; do not assume these options affect every profile.

field.label: Target Mode
field.help:
Target Mode is used only when a profile has no explicit <HOSTLIST:name> or <IPSET:name> placeholder.
All traffic — do not restrict target lists; Only listed targets — use YouTube, Telegram IPs and User lists; Auto-detect — also include the detected blocked-domain list.
This is engine target selection, not the IPFW interception port filter. Global Exclude Domains / Exclude IPSet remain independent.

field.label: YouTube Domains
field.help:
Source for <HOSTLIST:youtube>, one domain per line. example.com follows native subdomain matching; ^example.com matches the exact domain only; !example.com locally excludes it from this HOSTLIST; !^example.com excludes only the exact domain.
Pasted HTTP(S) URLs are normalized to hostnames. A wildcard domain cannot be combined with ! or ^; malformed/repeated modifiers are rejected with a line number. Local ! is not global Exclude Domains.

field.label: Telegram IPs
field.help: IPv4/IPv6 source for <IPSET:telegram> (shared with Voice). One IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR network per line. No hostnames, /0 or effective full-family coverage.

field.label: User Domains
field.help:
Source for <HOSTLIST:user>, one domain per line. example.com follows native subdomain matching; ^example.com matches the exact domain only; !example.com locally excludes it; !^example.com excludes the exact domain only.
Pasted HTTP(S) URLs are normalized to hosts. A wildcard cannot be combined with ! or ^. Duplicate conflicting rules and malformed modifiers are rejected with a line number. Local ! does not affect other profiles or global exclusions.

field.label: Exclude Domains
field.help:
Globally exclude these domains from DPI bypass, one domain per line. Use this when processing breaks connectivity to a specific site. This is separate from the local !example.com HOSTLIST modifier.
Do not enter ! or ^ here; modifiers are not supported in global Exclude Domains. Domain fields are handled by the native Python policy, which returns the failing line on invalid entries.

field.label: Exclude IPSet
field.help: Globally exclude these destination addresses from DPI bypass when native profile exclusions are enabled. One IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR per line; adjacent or overlapping networks are combined. No hostnames, zone indices, 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0 or equivalent full-family coverage. Leave empty for unchanged behavior; domain names belong in Exclude Domains.
